title: The May deadline was repeatedly oversimplified
text: The operative paragraph 16 has two stages: Prescribed Authority decides within one month of certified-copy production; elections follow within one month of that decision. It is not a standalone deadline of 13 June. Actual service and September decision are necessary to evaluate delay. If the reported 30 September decision is confirmed and paragraph 16 applies without modification, 30 October is a date to examine, not an independently established breach.

title: Three corrected dates materially affect the chronology
text: 20 May correction changes 19 October to 9 October 2025; 27 February to 7 February 2026; and 22 March 2026 to 22 March 2025. Original five-page versions and press reports can carry the old dates. The combined order is the better working reference. Paragraph 10 also prints 17195 rather than 17915; the correction order does not address this, so it is flagged rather than silently changed.

title: Some delays predate the current writ
text: The High Court itself records that elections notified on 21 February 2026 were stopped by an order of 23 February. That weakens any claim that every delay arose solely from AOA refusing to hold an election. It does not settle whether the October challenge was necessary, proportionate or resident-approved.

title: No public account of AOA legal spending
text: Residents publicly demanded accounts in October 2026 and alleged large collections in February 2026; the AOA called the allegations baseless and earlier defended its handling of the water crisis. No audited accounts or case-wise legal-expense statement is public, so neither the allegations nor the rebuttal can be checked from public material.

title: Why 2024 notices and later records name different presidents
text: Reporting on the 16 March 2024 election names Anjali Negi as president, matching the 2024 notices. The High Court judgment identifies Vinod Negi as president elected on 22 March 2025, matching later records. These are two different election results, not an inconsistency. Original result sheets are still not public.

title: A parking-right promise survives a zero-price label
text: One allotment exemplar itemises covered parking-1 as FOC, while its general clause 30 describes paid, first-come parking and a separate agreement. The separate sublease exemplar grants use of one covered parking in its schedule. These show specific promises need examination even where a separate parking price is zero. They do not establish that every flat has identical terms or decide enforceability.

title: The sublease expressly attempts to exclude parking from handover
text: Clause 30 says common services transfer to the association while parking and certain other facilities will not. The same deed contains a specific one-covered-space usage right and a clause requiring compliance with the Apartment Act/rules. This could help explain a services-versus-parking handover split, but it does not prove the clause is legally effective or the actual MOU adopted it. Obtain the signed MOU, declaration and parking inventory.

title: The 180-space gap is not the same as a 180-space regulatory deficit
text: The drawing records 1,312 homes and 1,132 proposed car spaces, a difference of 180. But it records minimum required car spaces as 1,003, so proposed inventory is 129 above that drawing minimum. These are different comparisons. Actual usable bays, approved later revisions and the total contractual promises still need audit. The sheet alone neither proves compliance today nor identifies owners without rights.

title: Multiple phase filenames are duplicate copies, not separate corroboration
text: Plan files filed under phases 1, 2 and 3 share one SHA-256 hash, and the sanction letter, land allotment and lease deed also appear under more than one phase. The common plan is whole-site in content. Repetition is not independent corroboration; a byte-level duplicate report is included.

title: Tower numbers differ between sales and sanction records
text: The sublease identifies a sanctioned Tower-9 with sales-plan Tower-7. Parking/right audits should match plot, sanctioned tower, sales tower and flat identifier before declaring mismatches. A similarly named Phase-3 document cannot be assumed to prove a current Tower-12 fact without mapping.

title: Road and designated-use restrictions are explicit
text: The Tower-10 certificate says no parking on road and use only as designated in the plan; changes require authority permission. The plan shows six-metre fire-tender roads and green areas. These documents justify checking actual occupation against approved geometry, not treating circulation/green space as spare permanent bays. The certificate covers Tower-10, not all towers.

title: MOU and multipoint issues were already on the 2024 agenda
text: July notice discusses CAM handover/MOU; December notice discusses MOU compliance and NPCL multipoint. Notices demonstrate acknowledgement and planned discussion, not completion, agreement terms, performance or legal fault. They provide a concrete document trail for requesting minutes, MOU annexures and implementation correspondence.

title: Separate proceedings must not be used as substitutes
text: The cheque matter, election writs, reported parking case and Tower-12 registry case concern different relief and parties. An order mentioning an AOA does not necessarily settle its election or accounts. Searches also surfaced unrelated cases where Hynish was only an address; those are excluded.

title: Insufficient support is not the same as forgery
text: Public reporting of the 30 September 2026 SDM decision says the challengers did not show support from one quarter of 1,211 eligible members. That is a finding about support, not a public finding that any signature was forged. Any forgery claim needs the order, the lists and a judicial or forensic finding.

title: Meter replacement and disconnection are separate questions
text: A meter may need replacing while the authority, notice and process for disconnection remain separate questions. The public resident account does not establish a cause of failure, who pays, or the legal basis for disconnection; no AOA or NPCL response is public. The wider multipoint conversion would change who supplies and bills each flat.

title: Hynish sits on a sub-plot of a much larger 2010 allotment
text: In March 2010 the Authority allotted the 204,000 sq m GH-08 plot to a Supertech-led consortium that included Panchsheel. Hynish is on GH-08A, a 30,000 sq m sub-plot leased to Panchsheel Buildtech in 2010. The sub-division record itself is not public.

title: The towers were built in four stages
text: The 2014 revised plan shows T1-T7 (stilt + 14) as already sanctioned and adds T8-T9 (stilt + 24), T10-T11 (stilt + 20) and T12 (stilt + 21). RERA data dates the three registered phases from 2014 to 2021, and a 2019 report had 10 towers occupied. Completion certificates for towers other than T10 are not public.

title: Public numbers about the society conflict
text: Unit totals: 1,312 (approved plan, most listings), 1,305 (builder website), 1,314 (one listing). Land: 7.41 acres / 30,000 sq m (plan) versus 7.00 acres (one listing). Plot: GH-08A (lease, plan, AOA website) versus GH-08 (a listing). Possession: May 2018 or January 2021 depending on the phase. The approved plan and registered lease are the stronger records. Allotted area of GH-08: 204,000 sq m (allotment letter) versus 209,557 sq m (Deed of Declaration).

title: Two election officers in 2025, at different times
text: Both reports fit the record. The 15 May 2025 DR order, reproduced in the official judgment, named the District Backward Class Welfare Officer. By 20 June 2025 the District Supply Officer had been nominated, and wrote to the AOA on 1 July asking for records and Rs 2.56 lakh. The High Court quashed the 15 May order on 1 August 2025.

title: Public coverage is mostly complaints
text: Almost all public news about Hynish carries residents' complaints. AOA statements appear in only a few items, and no public coverage of festivals or community events was found, though notices circulated to members show an annual "Hynish Day" on 7 September and a resident cricket league. The archive therefore says less about everyday community life than about disputes; that is a gap in public records, not a finding about the society.

title: Handover: 7 September 2024 by AOA records, without the electricity connection
text: AOA records give 7 September 2024; one news report said 6 September. Authority minutes show handover was directed by 15 July 2024, the electricity connection was still in the builder's name, and the MOU was "in progress". NPCL's 2026 notices are still addressed first to the builder. The signed MOU and inventory are not public.

title: The Tower-12 order was a direction to decide, not a registry order
text: The High Court's 9 April 2026 order, quoted in the Authority's 15 July order, asked the Authority to decide a representation within three months and expressed no view on the merits. Reports of "registry within 90 days" overstated it. The registry deadline is the Authority's own direction to the builder, depends on a T11/T12 completion certificate not yet issued, and covers Tower-11 and 12 home-buyers generally, not only the 29 petitioners.

title: NPCL's 2026 case for conversion rests on defaults, not consent
text: The 2020 notice used the consent route: multipoint unless a majority kept single point. The 2026 notices invoke "three defaults" under the 10 October 2024 tariff order (collection reports and a CA audit) and treat conversion as mandatory. Both 2026 notices are addressed to the builder, which still held the connection, and the AOA jointly; the notices do not establish which party defaulted, and the default letters themselves are not in hand.

title: The declaration does not list parking as a common area
text: The 2015 Deed of Declaration says no parking is provided in common areas, although its basement description includes parking. The annexures that would define limited-common or independent areas, where parking may have been placed, are not in the circulated copy. On this document the approved plan's 1,132 car spaces are not general common property; whether a reservation was lawful needs the missing annexures and the approved parking map.
